main_text.p: fensum, contra experientiam, contra rationem tueri conabitur. Hæc feceramus, & rem hanc extra dubium posueramus: Quid igitur ultra, molestis disputationibus Lectoris animum lassavimus? Scilicet ut Veritas jam victrix errori victo insultet, plurimumque rationum impetu jacentem veluti premat, & quasi pedibus conculcet. Adde quod vetissima[?] illa quæ ex Antiquis restituimus rerum Naturalium principia non absre[?] fuit, quemadmodum in omnibus, ita tota hac de visione speculatione, Naturæ testimonio comprobare. Quæcunque enim de visione docuimus fidem perhibent illis demonstrationibus, quibus libro secundo de materia probavimus, compositi naturalis partes igneas, ab ambientibus frigidis contineri, atque coërceri. Ergo ut in reliquis, ita hac in materia de visione videre est nostram doctrinam adeo consentientem, ut hæc de visu doctrina nostra inferat principia, & illis positis hanc doctrinam ostendere, ac tueri tam tibi sit in proclivi, quam imber est dum pluit, ut sic cum Plauto liceat concludere.
main_text.head: INTENTIO VI. De colore.
ARTICVLVS I. Argumentum.
main_text.p: AT tractationi de visu Colophonem addere-mus, visum est operæ pretium, doctrinam de coloribus adjungere, sine qua nemo perfectam naturæ visus cognitionem assequatur; nec satis videat, quomodo visio fiat, per ocularium radiorum factam ab objecto repercussionem. Aristo-telis,

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment ("fensum") and stays as printed. "vetissima" is uncertain: the long s is hard to read, so the word is marked [?]. "absre" is uncertain whether it is one word or two; marked [?]. The initial "A" of "AT" is a large initial and is joined to the word. The scan is slightly faded and skewed at the edges, but the body text is legible. The page ends on "Aristo-telis," with a line break and no catchword or signature visible. The running head was printed "DE VISV" and is given with u/v normalised as "DE VISU".
